solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Skirt that’s hitched up three hours before midday? (4)

indicatorNotes.hitched up: in a down clue, hitching something up lifts it, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: IX AM: nine o'clock in the morning, in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A woman hoists her long skirt early in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The skirt is long, so hitching it up sounds natural; the trick is writing 9 a.m. as IX AM.
annotation.definitionFit: Maxi is fashion shorthand for maximum, ankle-length; said of a skirt it names the garment itself.

entries.clue: Cook from Serbia going to pot (6)

indicatorNotes.going to pot: things going to pot fall into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: A chef from Serbia whose kitchen is falling apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a noun, a person from Serbia; it is the verb, and 'going to pot' doubles as a kitchen image.
annotation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid.

entries.clue: Talking bird (4)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Talking' is used as a noun here: talk, conversation.

blocks.note: casual talk; the gerund here is the noun sense, conversation
a small songbird of the thrush family, as in stonechat and whinchat

annotation.surface: A parrot or mynah that can speak.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, a bird that talks; split them and each means CHAT on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Chat is informal talking, and the chat is a family of small songbirds.

entries.clue: A central point exists for God (6)

blocks.note: as printed
the nub is the central point of a matter
is = exists

annotation.surface: A theological claim that a single central point exists for God.
annotation.walkthrough: The philosophical-sounding sentence is three plain pieces laid end to end.
annotation.definitionFit: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian god of the dead.

entries.clue: Intricate tune with viol played (8)

indicatorNotes.played: the tune and viol are played, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters; 'with' joins the two words

annotation.surface: A complicated melody performed on a viol.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word after 'Intricate' is musical, which hides that the tune and viol are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Involute means intricately complicated or entangled.

entries.clue: Pastry dish with fruit rising, make a mistake and it might be flat (4-1-5)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upward, so ERR becomes RRE

blocks.note: a pie is a pastry dish
the date is the fruit of a palm
to err is to make a mistake

annotation.surface: A baker's fruit pie rises, but get it wrong and it collapses flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising' and 'flat' look like baking terms for the pie; 'rising' works on the mistake, and 'flat' is a home.
annotation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second home, often a flat kept in town.

entries.clue: Express disapproval when husband tips instrument containing liquor (8)

indicatorNotes.containing: the harp holds the rum inside it
indicatorNotes.tips: the husband sits at the tip, the end, of the instrument

blocks.note: the harp, a stringed instrument
rum, a spirit
h = husband, as in genealogy abbreviations

annotation.surface: A wife tuts as her husband knocks over an instrument full of drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as knocking over; it places H at the tip of the assembled word.
annotation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to clear one's throat gruffly to show disapproval.

entries.clue: Image of suspect fool’s stolen (7)

blocks.note: a mug is a fool; 'fool's' = fool is, giving MUG'S
hot = stolen, as in hot goods

annotation.surface: A police photo of a fool whose goods were stolen.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is' and belongs to MUG, leaving HOT for 'stolen'.
annotation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a police photograph of a suspect's face.

entries.clue: Heart of local stolen by sister I love, Church diplomat (6)

indicatorNotes.Heart of: the heart of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a nun is a sister in a religious order
middle letter of loCal
as printed
love = O, a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: A nun makes off with a local's heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stolen by' here only joins pieces: C is taken by, and so follows, NUN.
annotation.definitionFit: A nuncio is the Pope's ambassador to a foreign government.

entries.clue: Family engaged in extravagant outdoor activity (6)

indicatorNotes.engaged in: the family is set inside the extravagant word

blocks.note: big = extravagant, as in a big gesture
kin = family

annotation.surface: A family taking part in some lavish open-air pursuit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' reads as a family taking part in something; its job is to put one piece inside another.
annotation.definitionFit: Biking is cycling, done outdoors.

entries.clue: More than one newspaper sold, I suspect, after club taken over (8)

indicatorNotes.taken over: turned over, so BAT reads backwards
indicatorNotes.I suspect: a suspect version of the words is a jumbled one
indicatorNotes.after: the anagram comes after the club

blocks.note: a bat is a club
anagram fodder SOLDI

annotation.surface: A publisher guesses several papers were sold after a football club takeover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' sounds like a speaker's aside; it is the anagram indicator, and 'I' also sits in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Tabloids are popular newspapers; the plural matches 'more than one'.

entries.clue: Walk off with sweet thing – and go too far? (4,3,7)

blocks.note: literally, walk off with a biscuit
the idiom for being the most outrageous

annotation.surface: Someone pockets a sweet and is told that is overstepping the mark.
annotation.walkthrough: A biscuit is what Americans call a cookie; 'take the biscuit' is the British version of 'take the cake'.
annotation.definitionFit: Taking the biscuit is being the most outrageous, going too far.

entries.clue: Sure to buy and sell supply, article going first (10)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
indicatorNotes.going first: the article is placed at the front

blocks.note: the indefinite article
anagram fodder TOBUY and SELL, 9 letters; 'and' joins them

annotation.surface: A trader's instruction: be sure to deal in stock, putting one item first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the noun, goods; it is the adverb from supple (flexibly), which makes it an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Absolutely!' is an emphatic yes, like 'sure!'.

entries.clue: Loud bang originally heralding flood (5)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the origin, so the start of the word, its first letter
indicatorNotes.heralding: B comes before, heralds, the next piece

blocks.note: first letter of Bang
a rash of something is a sudden flood of it

annotation.surface: A loud bang warning that a flood is coming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud bang' looks like one phrase; 'Loud' is the definition, in the sense of showy.
annotation.definitionFit: Brash and loud both mean showy and vulgar, as in loud clothes.

entries.clue: Way beyond some further thoughts I say! (4)

indicatorNotes.beyond: the way comes beyond, after, the thoughts

blocks.note: a PS, postscript, adds further thoughts to a letter
St = street, a way

annotation.surface: A letter writer tacks on an afterthought with an exclamation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like part of the phrase 'way beyond'; it is ST, placed beyond the postscript.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Psst!' is a whisper to catch attention, like 'I say!'.

entries.clue: Indian dish with duck filling half-baked roti (8)

indicatorNotes.filling: AND O goes inside the anagram
indicatorNotes.half-baked: not properly baked, so the letters of roti are mixed up

blocks.note: anagram fodder ROTI, rearranged as T…ORI
and = with
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of O

annotation.surface: A curry of duck with some undercooked flatbread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the meat of the dish; it is a zero. Roti is Indian flatbread, so every word stays in the kitchen.
annotation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven.

entries.clue: Vagabond, male seemingly caught? (5)

indicatorNotes.caught: the male is caught inside the trap

blocks.note: what M appears caught in: a trap, a snare
m = male

annotation.surface: A drifter, a man who looks as if he has been nabbed.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue only hints at the trap: 'seemingly caught' says M looks snared, and TRAMP is TRAP holding M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name someone with no home who roams from place to place.

entries.clue: Fencing move I don’t know: bother! (7)

blocks.note: 'pass' is what you say when you cannot answer a question
ado = fuss, bother

annotation.surface: A fencer admits ignorance of a move and curses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bother!' reads as an exclamation; it is the noun, trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: A passado is a forward thrust in fencing with one foot advanced.

entries.clue: Noble as Cockney kings and queens when stripped (4)

indicatorNotes.when stripped: stripping takes off the outer letters

blocks.note: PEARLY kings and queens, minus P and Y

annotation.surface: A London noble who is one of the Cockney kings and queens once undressed.
annotation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London charity figures in suits covered in pearl buttons; stripping PEARLY of its outside letters leaves EARL.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one rank of the British peerage, which 'Noble' as a noun covers.

entries.clue: Vile pants ending on floor alongside underwear for sea rover (4,4,6)

indicatorNotes.pants: as a verb, pants means is rubbish, so the letters come out wrong
indicatorNotes.ending on: the ending of a word is its final letter, so the ending on floor is its last letter
indicatorNotes.alongside: the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: long johns are long underpants
anagram fodder VILE
last letter of flooR

annotation.surface: Disgusting trousers left on the floor next to some underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as trousers or underpants beside 'underwear'; it is the British slang for rubbish, working as an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island.

entries.clue: Following spot of joyriding, crook in clink (6)

indicatorNotes.Following: following means coming after, so the crook's letters come after the spot
indicatorNotes.spot of: a spot, a small bit, of the word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Joyriding
a crook is a bend, an angle

annotation.surface: A criminal jailed after joyriding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crook' and 'clink' look like criminal and prison; crook is a bend, and clink is the definition, a metallic sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A jangle is a harsh clinking sound.

entries.clue: Babies leave a mess (6)

blocks.note: a brood of young animals born together to one mother
as a verb: to scatter rubbish about carelessly

annotation.surface: Babies making a mess.
annotation.walkthrough: The plural 'Babies' fits a litter, one brood of young animals.
annotation.definitionFit: A litter is a brood of newborns, and littering leaves rubbish about.

entries.clue: Lawyer worried about undecided strategy, ultimately (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so ATE is wrapped around TORN

blocks.note: ate = worried, as in 'what's eating you?'
torn between two choices
last letter of strategY

annotation.surface: A lawyer anxious about a strategy not yet settled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worried' is the past tense of worry: ATE, as in something ate at him.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, chiefly American: one qualified to act for clients in legal matters.

entries.clue: Old Tokyo, residential houses (4)

annotation.definitionNote: Yore is a noun, time long past; 'Old' matches it only in 'days of old' = 'days of yore'.

indicatorNotes.houses: the phrase houses, contains, the answer

blocks.note: tokYO REsidential

annotation.surface: A note on old Tokyo's residential housing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' reads as buildings; it is the verb, contains.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Of yore' and 'of old' both mean of long ago.

entries.clue: Where seven letters come in “dessert“? (6)

blocks.note: the seven letters T to Z close the alphabet, all following the nineteenth letter
British informal word for the pudding course

annotation.surface: A spelling question about how the letters of 'dessert' fall.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks push you to count the letters of 'dessert', which has seven; the seven letters are the end of the alphabet, AFTER S.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal for pudding, the course that comes after the main one.

entries.clue: Water seen when lid lifted from sewer (4)

indicatorNotes.when lid lifted from: in a down clue, the lid is the top letter, removed

blocks.note: DRAIN without its first letter D

annotation.surface: Water spotted coming out when a manhole cover is lifted.
annotation.walkthrough: The drain's lid is its top letter D.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one form water takes, falling as drops from cloud.

entries.clue: Blooming disheartened, fail test (6)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: loses its heart, the middle letters, leaving F and L

blocks.note: FaiL without its middle
an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: A dejected student curses after failing an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a British mild swearword; here it means flowery.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: 'blooming' as an adjective means in flower, and the answer means made of or like flowers.

entries.clue: Old country‘s gone to seed, so I heard (8)

indicatorNotes.gone to seed: run down and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Rumour that a former nation has declined.
annotation.walkthrough: 'So I heard' reads as a sound signal; it is the fodder. Rhodesia is now Zimbabwe and Zambia.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the country now Zimbabwe (and earlier also Zambia).
